question: Should OpenClaw add a bounded public exec approval timeout configuration contract, and which key, precedence, and maximum should be canonical?
rationale: The implementation is straightforward but the setting changes how long host-exec approvals remain actionable, so maintainers must choose the product/security contract before a repair PR is safe.

options.title: Approve bounded config contract
options.body: Add one supported approval-timeout key with strict validation, conservative bounds, explicit env/config precedence, and aligned docs/tests across agent, gateway, and CLI paths.

options.title: Keep fixed timeout
options.body: Close the configurable-timeout direction as not planned and rely on the current 30-minute default plus fail-fast fixes for unsupported approval surfaces.

options.title: Defer for security design
options.body: Keep this issue open until owners settle the approval-window threat model and whether environment overrides should be allowed at all.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded config contract
recommendation.body: Add one supported approval-timeout key with strict validation, conservative bounds, explicit env/config precedence, and aligned docs/tests across agent, gateway, and CLI paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the shared timeout constant and current default points to this owner path.
